title: Physician exam
description: STEMI, stroke lysis, transfusion, massive transfusion, chest drain, FAST, ventilation, antidotes, surgery indications, death.

questions.q: What is the alteplase dose in ischaemic stroke?
answers: 0.9 mg/kg, at most 90 mg, 10% as a bolus
0.6 mg/kg, at most 60 mg, 20% as a bolus
1.0 mg/kg, at most 100 mg, 15% as a bolus
0.9 mg/kg, at most 70 mg, 25% as a bolus

questions.q: Up to when can thrombolysis be given in stroke from the onset (clinical time)?
What is always needed before stroke thrombolysis?
answers: A head CT to rule out bleeding
A chest X-ray for the lungs
A blood group and a crossmatch
A FAST to rule out belly bleeding

questions.q: What happens when a haemorrhagic stroke is lysed?
answers: Nothing, the drug has no effect

questions.q: Which red cells are safe for a B Rh− recipient?
answers: AB Rh− and B Rh− units

questions.q: Which plasma can be given to anyone with an unknown group?
What may be given before the blood group is known in urgent bleeding?
answers: 0 Rh− red cells and AB plasma
AB Rh+ red cells and 0 plasma
A Rh+ red cells and B plasma

questions.q: What is the most dangerous complication of an incompatible transfusion?
When is it a massive transfusion in the system?
What must be done first to give group-specific, crossmatched blood?
answers: A blood group lab, then a crossmatch
A chest CT, then an ECG
A glucose, then a urine test
A FAST, then a control X-ray

questions.q: What does too much blood, given too fast, cause after a small loss?
Where is the chest drain inserted?
answers: 2nd intercostal space in the mid-clavicular line
7th–8th intercostal space in the scapular line
Below the sternum at the xiphoid process

questions.q: Where is needle decompression done in tension pneumothorax?
When is a thoracotomy needed for a haemothorax?
answers: When more than 1500 ml comes from the drain
When less than 200 ml comes from the drain
For every haemothorax, before any drain
Only when the patient gets no oxygen

questions.q: Which FAST window shows the fluid of a splenic injury?
Which FAST window shows the fluid of a liver injury?
What does missing lung sliding in the lung window show?
What is the urgent treatment of cardiac tamponade?
answers: A high IV dose of furosemide
A chest drain on the right side

questions.q: What is the first-line treatment of STEMI when available?
answers: A chest drain and a needle

questions.q: When is nitroglycerin contraindicated in STEMI?
answers: When a right ventricular (inferior) infarct is suspected
When the systolic BP is above 140 mmHg
When the patient already took aspirin that day
When the SpO₂ falls below 95% on the reading

questions.q: Which complication is typical of an inferior STEMI?
What are the ECG signs of an inferior STEMI?
answers: ST elevation in II, III, aVF, reciprocal in I, aVL
ST elevation in V1–V4, reciprocal in II and III
ST depression in every lead in the same way
A wide QRS and peaked T waves in every lead

questions.q: What is the first step in NSTEMI instead of PCI?
answers: Discharge and a GP check-up after one week
A chest drain and a FAST to rule out shock

questions.q: At what potassium level is hyperkalaemia treatment urgent?
answers: Above 6.5 mmol/l or with ECG changes

questions.q: What protects the heart at once in hyperkalaemia?
What is the antidote of paracetamol poisoning?
What treats organophosphate poisoning?
What is the antidote of beta-blocker poisoning?
What is the antidote of methanol poisoning?
What is the antidote of cyanide poisoning?
What is the specific treatment of digoxin poisoning?
answers: A high dose of IV calcium

questions.q: What is the basic treatment of carbon monoxide poisoning?
What is given in TCA poisoning with a wide QRS?
On the ventilator, what improves oxygenation most?
answers: Raising the FiO₂ and the PEEP

questions.q: What mainly sets the EtCO₂ on a ventilator?
answers: The dose and rate of the noradrenaline

questions.q: What is the downside of a PEEP that is too high?
answers: It reduces venous return, the blood pressure falls
It suddenly raises the glucose and the lactate
It takes away the patient's pain and anxiety
It speeds up the kidneys and the urine output

questions.q: What happens when a ventilated patient is not sedated?
answers: They fight the machine, SpO₂ falls, heart rate rises
They wake faster and can be extubated at once
Nothing, the ventilation works just the same
The machine stops by itself and alarms

questions.q: What is the target of noradrenaline titration in septic shock?
answers: A mean arterial pressure of at least 65 mmHg
A systolic blood pressure of at least 180 mmHg
A heart rate of exactly under 60 per minute

questions.q: Who may record a death in the hospital?
What must be given when a death is recorded?
answers: The time, the cause with an ICD code, the circumstances
Only the patient's name and the hospital's name
The patient's blood group and the lab results
The last medicine's dose and the time it was given

questions.q: What happens to the body when nobody takes it to the morgue for 20 minutes?
answers: The NPC morgue staff takes it, no points
The body stays in the corridor forever
The patient comes back to life by itself
The system deletes the case with an error

questions.q: What do you do with a patient who is dead on arrival?
answers: Record the death, then push to the morgue
An immediate CT and a full lab for the cause
A discharge, handed over to the relatives
An S1 transfer to another hospital

questions.q: Who can send a patient to the operating theatre?
answers: A physician; a resident asks, a physician approves
Any nurse, even without the treating doctor
Only the ambulance leader from the tablet
Only the chief, and only after appointment

questions.q: When may a resident send to the theatre without approval?
answers: When no physician is on duty
When the operation is under 5 minutes

questions.q: Which operation may go ahead on the waiting place?
answers: Every operation, in the order of arrival

questions.q: What raises the risk of an operation's outcome?
answers: High shock index, delay, untreated findings, age
That the patient was brought in by ambulance
That a full lab was done before the operation
That the treating doctor is of chief rank

questions.q: What do you do when the operation ends with a complication?
answers: Discharge at once with a painkiller
An S2 transfer to the nearest hospital

questions.q: With a splenic injury and unstable circulation, what is the definitive care?
answers: A cast and a control X-ray
A chest drain on the left

questions.q: Epidural haematoma with mass effect: what is the treatment?
In an unstable pelvic fracture, what is the first step in the shock room?
answers: A cast on the lower leg

questions.q: What does an S1 transfer mean?
answers: An immediate transfer, only a physician asks
A transfer within 3 hours, residents too
Taking the patient home by taxi, for free
Taking the body to the morgue by an NPC

questions.q: What happens to a transfer when no suitable unit is signed in?
answers: Automatic transfer after 3 min (S1) or 10 min (S2)
The request is deleted, the patient stays on the ward
The system calls an NPC ambulance to the scene
A hospital staff member must take the patient

questions.q: What does the target hospital get as the transfer's handover text?
How long is the ICU stay of a stable patient?
Who is alerted when an ICU patient worsens and there is no treating doctor?
What is the first step in anaphylactic shock?
What does DKA look like in the lab?
answers: High glucose, low pH, negative base excess
Low glucose, high pH, positive base excess
Normal glucose, high troponin, high CK
High haemoglobin, low potassium, high INR

questions.q: What does a high D-dimer with chest pain and tachycardia point to?
Where in the hospital may alteplase be given?
answers: In the shock room or the ICU
In the corridor, on any trolley
Only on the ward, at the bedside
Only in the CT, during the scan

questions.q: When may a massive transfusion be ordered?
answers: From physician rank, in the shock room or ICU
From nurse rank, anywhere in the hospital
From resident rank, only in the corridor
Only with the chief's approval on the PC
